subject: Audit & Access log egress options, retention windows, and deletion proof
messages:
From: John Miller <john.miller@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-08-01 09:12 -0400
Subject: Audit/access logs: export and retention capabilities (EU tenant)

Hi Karthik,

Quick question from our compliance team: for our EU tenant can you confirm the following?

1) How long are access logs and audit logs retained by default on Redwood hosted?
2) Can we export a full month-long slice of logs (audit + access) to our S3 bucket for offsite archival? What formats and delivery methods do you support?
3) If we ask for deletion of a tenant, what proof will you provide that those logs were removed from your systems (backups, archives, caches)?

We just want to document the flow before we proceed with the annual audit.

Thanks,
John
John Miller
Director, Compliance
Acme Health
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: John Miller <john.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, sofia_ivanova@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-08-01 11:04 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit/access logs: export and retention capabilities (EU tenant)

Hi John — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR: yes, we can export and provide deletion attestation; details and options below.

Retention (hosted):
- Access logs (HTTP requests, token/route-level metadata): default retention 90 days.
- Audit logs (control plane events, admin actions, role changes): default retention 365 days.

Export options:
- Formats: NDJSON (recommended), CSV (columnar export), Parquet (for analytics).
- Delivery: S3 (recommended), GCS, Azure Blob, or SFTP. We support direct push (server-side copy) or pre-signed upload if you prefer to pull.
- Scope: you can request a time window (start/end). For hosted tenants we can extract the full retained window (i.e., up to the configured retention) as a bulk snapshot. For windows older than retention we cannot reconstruct deleted events.

Deletion & attestation:
- For tenant deletion requests we perform: (a) tombstone soft-delete, (b) background sweep to remove logs from hot storage and KV caches, (c) purge from long-term object stores per lifecycle policy.
- Proof: we provide a signed deletion manifest that includes object keys removed, timestamps, and an export of the deletion audit record. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can additionally perform customer-observed erase (on-prem) or provide a KMS-wrapped certificate for the deletion operation.

I'll attach the export-format matrix and a short runbook. Let me loop in Laura for SLA/production constraints and Sofia for cross-border considerations.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
To: John Miller <john.miller@acmehealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: sofia_ivanova@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-08-02 08:27 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit/access logs: export and retention capabilities (EU tenant)

Hi John — a couple of operational notes to set expectations: 

- Export throughput: typical bulk export of 30 days (audit + access) for a medium tenant takes 2–8 hours depending on size; very large tenants may need a staging window and chunked delivery.
- Retention configuration: customers on Dedicated/Private can extend retention beyond hosted defaults via config (we recommend lifecycle tiers to control cost).
- Export consistency: we produce a manifest and a per-file checksum (SHA256). For S3 delivery we can write directly into a customer-controlled bucket via an IAM role; for SFTP we push to a customer path and provide a signed delivery receipt.

If you want, we can schedule a short run-through where we initiate a small test export (48 hours of logs) into your S3 test bucket to validate IAM, paths, and parsing.

-Laura
Principal Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: John Miller <john.miller@acmehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-08-02 13:41 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit/access logs: export and retention capabilities (EU tenant)

Thanks — that helps. A few follow ups from our side: 

1) For the deletion manifest, will Redwood include a signed timestamp from your KMS and an index of the S3 object keys you removed? Our auditors expect a cryptographic proof.
2) What is the SLA for completing a tenant-level deletion? We need an upper bound (hours/days) for our playbooks.
3) If we keep an offsite archive longer than your hosted retention, will you honor requests to re-ingest logs for investigation if we bring them back later?

Agree that a short test export would be useful — can we do that next week?

John
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.example.com
To: John Miller <john.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-08-03 15:40 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit/access logs: export and retention capabilities (EU tenant)

Hi John — quick answers to your follow-ups: 

1) Deletion manifest: yes. We provide a signed manifest that includes KMS-signed metadata (operation id, operator, timestamp), list of object keys removed, and a signed hash of the manifest. That meets most auditor requirements; we can add an extended signature if you require external timestamping (e.g., RFC3161).

2) Deletion SLA: standard tenant-level deletion completes within 14 days end-to-end for hosted tenants (this covers background sweeps and object store lifecycle expiries). We provide an interim status report at 72 hours and a final attestation when complete. For Dedicated customers this can be accelerated to 72 hours with a proctored erase.

3) Re-ingest: Redwood does not reconstitute logs that have been deleted from our systems. If you maintain your offsite archive we can help validate and re-index those files into your analytics environment, but we cannot restore deleted hosted-retention content from our deleted backups.

Next steps: we'll set up a 48-hour test export into your S3 test bucket and provide the sample manifest and checksums. Please share the bucket name and preferred delivery method (direct write via IAM role or pre-signed URLs).

Regards,
Sofia
Security & Compliance Specialist, Redwood Inference
